FAQ.heading:
Before we begin,
a few answers.
FAQ.description:
Questions before getting started?
From our process and pricing to ongoing support,
here are the answers to help you plan ahead.

company.question: What kind of company is GRIDS?
company.answer: GRIDS is a software development company building websites, applications, business systems, and AI solutions. We work with you to understand your goals and everyday challenges, then turn them into useful products—from planning through development.

services.question: What can you build, and when should I get in touch?
services.answer: We build websites, online stores, web and mobile apps, CRM and admin systems, workflow automation, and AI tools that use your company’s knowledge. Get in touch when you want to launch a service, connect scattered information, or reduce repetitive work.

pricing.question: How do you determine development costs?
pricing.answer: Costs depend on the features, design scope, integrations, and timeline. We clarify the scope during consultation before providing an estimate. If you have a set budget, we can explore a phased approach that starts with your priorities.

quality.question: How do you ensure project quality?
quality.answer: We agree on the scope and review criteria upfront, then review progress and deliverables together at key stages. An 80% refund policy also applies under agreed conditions. We explain the eligibility criteria and process during consultation.

starting.question: Can I book a consultation if I only have an idea?
starting.answer: Yes. You do not need a finished brief. Tell us about the problem you want to solve, who the service is for, and any examples you have in mind. We can work through the essential features and priorities together.

support.question: What does maintenance cost after launch?
support.answer: Costs depend on the size of the service, its operating environment, and the support you need. We distinguish running costs, such as hosting, from maintenance and feature development, then agree on the support that makes sense for your business.

integration.question: Can you connect to our existing systems?
integration.answer: Integration depends on the APIs, permissions and data structures available in your current systems. Tell us which tools you use and the workflows you want to connect. We’ll review what can be integrated and identify any additional work before defining the scope.

preparation.question: What should we prepare before a consultation?
preparation.answer: It helps to outline your goals, users, essential features, target timeline and budget. Share reference sites and any systems you already use. We’ll clarify the logo, copy, images and other materials needed as we define the scope.

timeline.question: How is the project timeline decided?
timeline.answer: We assess the features, page count, design complexity, integrations and readiness of your materials. Together, we set milestones for planning, design, development and review. If you have a target launch date, we can consider releasing the essential features first.

communication.question: How do we communicate and review progress?
communication.answer: Before starting, we agree on contacts, communication channels and the review process. We review deliverables at key stages and assess how requested changes affect scope and timing before implementing them. Consolidating feedback in one place helps keep reviews clear.

scopeChanges.question: Can we change features or designs during the project?
scopeChanges.answer: We first check whether a change falls within the agreed scope. For additions or major design changes, we explain the impact on cost and timing and proceed after agreement. Defining priorities and revision scope at the outset helps reduce unexpected changes.

externalCosts.question: Are there costs outside the project quote?
externalCosts.answer: Third-party costs such as domains, hosting, API usage, payment fees and paid assets are separate. Some depend on usage. We review the services and expected usage your product requires and distinguish these costs from development fees.

assistant.question: How do we onboard a new client?
assistant.answer:
New client onboarding follows three steps.

1. Confirm the contract — Check scope, timeline, and payment terms, then add the client to your CRM.
2. Assign an owner — Name the project lead and client contact. Share a checklist of required files and access permissions.
3. Run the kickoff — Agree on goals, priorities, and milestones, then send meeting notes and the first action items.

Before you start, have the contract, requirements, and contact details ready. I can also draft the welcome email for your client.

delivery.title: Resolve a delivery question from order records
delivery.hint: Order system × shipping policy × support ticket
delivery.question: Hanbit Living received only part of order HB-1042. Check dispatch records and policy for the remaining quantity and any extra shipping charge.
delivery.answer:
I checked the order system, shipping policy and customer support ticket.

The order contains 12 units. Ten have shipped; two are still being inspected at the warehouse. The current record estimates dispatch within two business days.

The company covers additional shipping when an order is split for operational reasons, so the customer has no extra shipping charge.

For ticket CS-208, the answer is: “The remaining two units will ship separately after inspection, at no additional shipping cost.” The actual arrival date needs to be checked once tracking is available.
